title: Weather & Health
description: Describe the weather, talk about illnesses, and describe symptoms to a doctor.

vocabulary.source: I need to go to the doctor

grammar.title: HACER for weather — impersonal expressions
grammar.content:
Spanish uses the verb **hacer** (to do/make) to describe weather conditions. This verb is impersonal — it only appears in the third person singular: **hace**.

Weather expressions with 'hacer':
- **Hace sol** — It is sunny (literally: 'the sun makes')
- **Hace frío** — It is cold
- **Hace calor** — It is hot
- **Hace viento** — It is windy
- **Hace buen tiempo** — The weather is nice
- **Hace mal tiempo** — The weather is bad

Other weather verbs that change:
- **Llueve** — It is raining
- **Nieva** — It is snowing
- **Graniza** — It is hailing

**Estar + adjective** for weather:
- **Está nublado** — It is cloudy
- **Está despejado** — It is clear
- **Está lloviendo** — It is raining (progressive)

To ask about weather: ¿Qué tiempo hace? or ¿Cómo está el clima?
examples: Hace calor en verano. (It is hot in summer.)
Hace frío hoy. (It is cold today.)
Hoy llueve mucho. (It is raining a lot today.)
Está nublado, creo que va a llover. (It is cloudy, I think it is going to rain.)
grammar.note: Remember: 'hacer' weather expressions are ALWAYS third person singular — they never change form. 'Hace' is used for all weather descriptions except when using the progressive (-iendo) or adjective forms with 'estar'.

grammar.title: TENER + noun for physical states
grammar.content:
Spanish uses **tener** (to have) to express many physical states and conditions, rather than 'to be' like English.

Key expressions:
- **tener fiebre** — to have a fever
- **tener calor** — to feel hot
- **tener frío** — to feel cold
- **tener sueño** — to feel sleepy
- **tener hambre** — to be hungry
- **tener sed** — to be thirsty
- **tener miedo** — to be afraid
- **tener prisa** — to be in a hurry

Conjugation:
- yo **tengo** fiebre
- tú **tienes** frío
- él/ella **tiene** sed
- nosotros **tenemos** hambre
- ellos **tienen** sueño

Note: 'tener calor' and 'tener frío' are different from 'hace calor' and 'hace frío'. Use 'tener' when talking about how YOU feel, and 'hace' when describing the weather.
examples: Tengo frío, ¿puedes cerrar la ventana? (I'm cold, can you close the window?)
El niño tiene miedo de los médicos. (The child is afraid of doctors.)
grammar.note: These are some of the most important phrases for A1.2. You will use them constantly — especially 'tener fiebre', 'tener frío', and 'tener calor'.

grammar.title: ME DUELE / ME DUELEN — I have pain
grammar.content:
To express pain or aches in Spanish, use **doler** (to hurt/to cause pain) with an indirect object pronoun: **me, te, le, nos, les**.

The verb agrees with what is hurting:
- **Me duele** la cabeza. (My head hurts.) — singular
- **Me duelen** los ojos. (My eyes hurt.) — plural

Structure: me/te/le + duele/dueles + [body part]

Common expressions:
- **Me duele la cabeza** — I have a headache
- **Me duele la garganta** — I have a sore throat
- **Me duele el estómago** — I have a stomachache
- **Me duelen las piernas** — My legs hurt
- **Me duele el diente** — I have a toothache
- **Me duele la espalda** — I have back pain

Other pain expressions:
- **Me siento mareado/a** — I feel dizzy
- **Me siento enfermo/a** — I feel sick
- **Tengo dolor de...** — I have pain in... (alternative to 'me duele')
examples: Me duele la cabeza. (I have a headache.)
Me duelen los ojos porque leo mucho. (My eyes hurt because I read a lot.)
Mi madre tiene dolor de espalda. (My mother has back pain.)
grammar.note: The verb 'doler' follows the same pattern as 'gustar': the thing that hurts is the subject, and the person feeling it is the indirect object.

pronunciation.title: Weather vocabulary pronunciation
pronunciation.content:
Weather words often contain the 'll', 'rr', and 'j' sounds. Practice these carefully:

- **llueve** — 'yue-beh' (ll = y sound)
- **niebla** — 'nyeh-blah' (ie = one syllable)
- **granizo** — 'grah-nee-soh'
- **tormenta** — 'tor-men-tah'
- **helada** — 'eh-lah-dah'
- **neblina** — 'neh-blee-nah'

Remember: vowels are always short and clear. Never add an 'uh' sound at the end of Spanish words.
examples: Llueve en Madrid. (It is raining in Madrid.)
Hace mucho frío en invierno. (It is very cold in winter.)
La temperatura es alta. (The temperature is high.)

pronunciation.title: Health vocabulary pronunciation
pronunciation.content:
Health terms often have 'c' before 'e/i' (sounds like 'th' in Spain, 's' elsewhere) and the trilled 'rr':

- **fiebre** — 'fee-e-breh'
- **cabeza** — 'ca-beh-sah' (Spain) / 'ca-beh-sah' (Latin America)
- **garganta** — 'gar-gan-tah'
- **estómago** — 'es-toh-mah-go'
- **resfriado** — 'reh-free-ah-doh'
- **gripe** — 'gree-peh'

The accent mark on 'estómago' indicates which syllable is stressed: es-TÓ-ma-go.
examples: Tengo fiebre y dolor de cabeza. (I have a fever and a headache.)
Me duele la garganta. (My throat hurts.)
Necesito ir al médico. (I need to go to the doctor.)

exercises.question: What is 'el dolor de cabeza' in English?
How do you say 'the flu' in Spanish?
Which is correct? '___ hace frío hoy.'
What does 'Me duele la cabeza' mean?
How do you say 'it's sunny' in Spanish?
Which is correct? 'Me ___ los ojos.' (my eyes hurt)
How do you say 'to cough' in Spanish?
'Yo tengo ___' means 'I am hungry'. Which word fills the blank?
How do you say 'the doctor' in Spanish?
Which verb form is correct for weather? 'Hoy ___ calor.'

dialogues.title: At the doctor's office
dialogues.content:
Doctor: ¿Qué le pasa?
Patient: Me duele la cabeza y tengo fiebre.
Doctor: ¿Cuánto tiempo lleva así?
Patient: Desde ayer. También toso mucho.
Doctor: Parece un resfriado. Tome medicina y descanse.
Patient: ¿Necesito una receta?
Doctor: Sí, le doy una receta para la medicina.
